questions.q: What share of Americans are illiterate or barely literate?
a: One-third
One-tenth
One-half
One-fifth
questions.why: Lesson 1 calls illiteracy a growing epidemic and says one-third of the US population is completely or barely literate.

questions.q: How long is the TV on daily in the average US household?
a: About seven hours
About two hours
About four hours
About ten hours
questions.why: Lesson 1 cites estimates that American households keep the television on roughly seven hours daily.

questions.q: What does Hedges say television does to reality?
a: It distorts it while offering easy, fake excitement
It reveals it more clearly than books can
It has no effect on how viewers see the world
It makes viewers more skeptical of advertising
questions.why: Lesson 1 says TV is excellent at distorting reality, presenting predictable content and an illusion of excitement.

questions.q: How does screen culture endanger democracy?
a: It validates only those on screen and normalizes surveillance
It gives too much airtime to serious policy debates
It encourages citizens to read more newspapers
It makes politicians less concerned with image
questions.why: Lesson 2 says TV validates those who appear on it and normalizes constant monitoring by government and corporations.

questions.q: What happens when education abandons the humanities?
a: Students lose the moral reasoning a society needs
Students become more skilled at technical jobs
Colleges produce more philosophers than managers
Debate and ethics become central to every course
questions.why: Lesson 3 says without the humanities, students miss the ethical and philosophical thinking needed to keep a culture from decaying.
